sector: Agricultural implements (Super Seeders, straw reapers, rotavators, laser levellers, biomass machines)
headline: Proforma revenue grew 63% in FY26 to Rs 414.0 cr with an EBITDA margin of 13.5%, but the business only combined on 1-Apr-2025, one customer is 25% of revenue and FY26 operating cash flow was 8.6% of PAT as stock built up; at the Rs 155.78 peer-median reference the price asks for a continuation of that growth.
red_flags: Proforma revenue Rs 253.8 cr to Rs 414.0 cr (+63.1%); EBITDA Rs 36.8 cr to Rs 55.7 cr; PAT Rs 20.7 cr to Rs 31.4 cr (pp. 92, 158)
Promoters' two proprietorships were taken over on 1-Apr-2025 at carrying value; restated FY25 (Rs 95.9 cr) is not comparable with FY26 (pp. 247, 387)
Seth Agro Industries is 25.21% of FY26 revenue; top 10 customers 50.04%; top supplier only 7.94% (pp. 261, 39)
FY26 CFO Rs 2.7 cr vs PAT Rs 31.4 cr; finished goods Rs 43.2 cr vs Rs 1.9 cr; cumulative CFO/PAT 69.7% (pp. 88, 474)
Rs 300 cr fresh issue: 66.7% identified (Rs 110 cr working capital, Rs 71.7 cr capex on promoter-leased land, Rs 18.5 cr debt); no capex order placed (pp. 124, 129)
Net debt Rs 119.4 cr (2.14x EBITDA); borrowings Rs 164.1 cr by 31-Aug-2026; subsidy-linked demand and Q4 seasonality (pp. 56, 34)
reference_note: Rs 155.78 = FY26 basic EPS Rs 5.64 x 27.62x, the median of the three listed peers the issuer names (pp. 154-156). It is an assumption, not a price band. The only priced issue, the Oct-2025 allotment against the promoters' businesses at Rs 33.63 after bonus and split (pp. 163, 388), was non-cash and is not used.

strengths: Proforma revenue CAGR 41.3% over FY24-FY26; industry 10.2% over FY23-26 per the issuer-commissioned CARE report (pp. 92, 248)
ROCE 31.1% and interest cover 5.03x in FY26 (p. 158)
Cash tax 26.1% of cumulative PBT; no deferred-tax cushion (p. 87)
Top supplier 7.94% and top 10 suppliers 40.53% of FY26 purchases, down from 76.68% (p. 39)
20+ products and 192 SKUs; 233 dealers and 12 distributors across 20 states (pp. 246, 247)
weaknesses: Seth Agro Industries 25.21% of FY26 revenue (p. 261)
Northern states 68.04% and Central states 25.95% of revenue (p. 29)
Top three products 64.40% of FY26 revenue (p. 29)
FY26 CFO Rs 26.85 m vs PAT Rs 313.90 m (p. 88)
Audit trail in the accounting software only from Jan-2026 (p. 416)
opportunities: Indian farm equipment market Rs 1,397 bn FY26 to Rs 1,876 bn FY30, 7.7% CAGR, issuer-commissioned estimate (p. 250)
Dehlon expansion adds 29,000 units to 4,000, due Mar-2028 (pp. 137, 143)
Biomass briquette and pellet machines for crop-residue conversion (pp. 252, 253)
R&D team of 46 and three patents (p. 246)
threats: Demand depends on CRM and SMAM subsidies, with past delays in state payments (pp. 56, 57)
Q4 is a seasonally weak quarter (p. 34)
Group company Goodfield Technology has common pursuits with the issuer (p. 30)
Promoters were disqualified as directors from Sep-2020 to Oct-2021; compounding applications filed (p. 37)
Larger tractor OEMs (Escorts Kubota, VST, Indo Farm) are the only listed comparables (p. 156)

flags: AMBER: DCF and relative diverge by -43.0% - the divergence is the finding; name its cause
AMBER: TV above 75% of EV - DCF is mostly a terminal guess
model.reverse_dcf: Current free cash flow is negative, so no multiple can be stated: the price assumes cash generation improves from here.
